note: The venue directory (data/venues.json) is baked from OpenStreetMap by scripts/build-venues.js - real places, real coordinates. This file is the editorial layer: venue blurbs/tags, walks and sights, plus any hand-curated events (verified real ones only, with a source URL). Day-to-day events come from venues themselves through the self-service API. See DATA.md.

church-inn.blurb: Hilltop pub beside St Chad’s, brewing its own ales in the yard. Home of the Saddleworth Morris Men — the Rushcart weekend ends here with dancing and gurning.

cross-keys.blurb: Stone-flagged moorside local up the hill from the village, long famous for its folk nights and its welcome for walkers straight off the tops.

waggon-inn.blurb: Coaching inn on Uppermill High Street — hearty food, cask ales and live music at the heart of the village.

commie.blurb: The Commercial — 'the Commie' to everyone — a friendly boozer at the top end of the High Street with a busy calendar of open mics and beer festivals.

hare-and-hounds.blurb: Traditional stone pub on the High Street corner — proper pints, sport on the telly and a fireside seat in winter.

saddleworth-museum.blurb: The story of the Saddleworth villages — mills, moors, brass bands and the Rushcart — in an old mill beside the canal, with a gallery of local art.

uppermill-civic-hall.blurb: The village's big room — markets, fairs, concerts and community events all year round, plus term-time regulars from Saddleworth School of Dance to Little Voices drama and singing (midweek after school).

old-bell-inn.blurb: Eighteenth-century coaching inn holding a world-record gin collection behind its glowing gin emporium bar — plus rooms and a busy restaurant.

white-lion.blurb: Village pub in the heart of Delph, a stone's throw from the brook — quiz nights, cask ale and no airs and graces.

millgate-arts-centre.blurb: Saddleworth's little theatre — home of the Saddleworth Players, plus comedy, music and film nights through the year. Delph Library lives inside the building; the bar opens around show times and tickets are sold online or on 01457 876644.
millgate-arts-centre.hours: Library: Tu-Th 14:00-17:00; Fr-Sa 10:00-13:00 · bar open around shows

swan.blurb: Eighteenth-century pub on Dobcross Square, all low beams and stone floors — known to locals as the Top House, and a favourite of brass banders on Whit Friday.

navigation-inn.blurb: Canalside pub by the old wool warehouse where the narrowboats once loaded — pints on the towpath in summer.

grandpa-greenes.blurb: Award-winning luxury ice cream served right on the canal towpath — deckchairs, ducks and sundaes with a view of the moors. Closes 2 September 2026 for a complete rebuild in reclaimed Cheshire brick with oak trusses; reopening expected winter 2026/27 — confirm nearer the time.

railway-inn.blurb: Opposite Greenfield station and the first pint off the Transpennine train — real ales, live music and a proper landlord's welcome.

king-william-iv.blurb: Friezland's local on the Oldham road — curry nights, quizzes and a beer garden under the hills.

boarshurst-band-club.blurb: Home of the Boarshurst Silver Band and the valley's Sunday-night brass concerts — visiting bands from across the North play here nearly every week.

saddleworth-cricket-bowling-and-tennis-c.blurb: The big sports club at Well-i-Hole — cricket on summer Saturdays, tennis courts and crown greens all season, and the valley's big bonfire and fireworks every November.

white-hart.blurb: Lydgate's celebrated dining pub on the brow of the hill — modern British cooking, a charcuterie of its own and views back across the whole of Saddleworth.

rams-head-inn.blurb: A 400-year-old dining inn alone on the moor road above Denshaw, with its own farm shop and tea rooms next door.

printers-arms.blurb: Denshaw's village pub — steak nights, cask ale and a warm room when the weather comes over the tops.

saddleworth-golf-club.blurb: A moorside course above the valley — every fairway has a view, and the 19th hole has an open fire. Visitors and societies welcome.

dovestone-sailing-club.blurb: Dinghies on Dovestone under Alderman and Alphin — one of the most dramatic places to sail in the North. Beginners' sessions all season.

three-crowns.blurb: High on the Oldham road at Scouthead with one of the best sunset views in the borough — beer festivals and big Sunday dinners.

farrars-arms.blurb: Roadside pub between Grasscroft and Lydgate with a sunny front terrace, acoustic sessions and a good line in Sunday lunches.

dinnerstone.blurb: Closed at the start of 2026 after twenty years. Acquisition by the Muse Group (Muse Bar & Eatery and the Farrars Arms) confirmed August 2026 — reopening date, name and hours still to be announced. Watch this space.

tame-valley-tennis-and-squash-club.blurb: Tennis, squash, racketball and pickleball on Greenbridge Lane — pay-and-play courts, coaching, and padel courts arriving from spring 2026.

uppermill-conservative-club.blurb: The Con Club on the High Street — function room, snooker, and the local Rock Choir’s concert venue of choice.

saddleworth-pool-and-leisure-centre.blurb: The village pool — lane, public and family swims through the week (term and holiday timetables differ), Oldham Active's Rainbow learn-to-swim programme (book via the portal — lesson times aren't published), and home water of Saddleworth Sharks swimming club.

delph-band-club.blurb: Home of Delph Band and its thriving youth wing — Tooters, Training Band and Youth Band rehearse Saturday mornings (contact via delphyouthband.com). Senior band rehearses Monday & Wednesday evenings.

springhead-liberal-club.name: Springhead Sports & Social Club
springhead-liberal-club.blurb: The old Springhead Liberal Club — 'the Libs' to locals, on this site since 1902 — now the Sports & Social Club at 136 Oldham Road, fielding Springhead SSC in the Saddleworth Pool League with the crown-green bowling club alongside. Oldham Fly Fishing Club — trout on Piethorne and Kitcliffe reservoirs — holds its meetings here.

j-w-buckley-ltd.name: Buckleys
j-w-buckley-ltd.blurb: J W Buckley's — family bakers on the High Street, baking pies, bread and sandwiches on site for the shop counter and the wholesale rounds alike.

tyromancer.blurb: Uppermill's new cheesemonger — a counter of British and continental cheeses with deli bits to match, opened on the High Street in 2026.

golden-house.blurb: Greenfield's chippy — Chinese dishes and fish-and-chips from the counter on Greenbridge Lane.

saddleworth-rangers-arlfc.blurb: Community rugby league at Shaw Hall Bank Road — Rangers Tots and junior teams from U7s to U18s through to the open-age first team. Club office 01457 876077 (11:00–14:00).

customVenues.name: The Diggle Hotel
customVenues.blurb: Stone free-house in the fold of the hills by the Standedge Tunnel end — freshly refurbished and reopened in July 2026. The bar is pouring; the kitchen (and the pies) return soon.
customVenues.hours: Mo-Tu from 15:00; We off; Th from 15:00; Fr-Su from 12:00 (bar)

customVenues.name: RSPB Dove Stone
customVenues.blurb: Moorland, woods and open water under the gritstone edges — peregrines and mountain hares up top, family trails around the reservoir. Car park and accessible paths at the bottom.

customVenues.name: Brownhill Countryside Centre
customVenues.blurb: Little canalside visitor centre at Brownhill Bridge — wildlife displays, family activities and the starting point for gentle towpath wanders.

customVenues.name: Castleshaw Roman Fort
customVenues.blurb: Grass-covered earthworks of a Roman fort guarding the pass over Standedge since AD 79, above the Castleshaw reservoirs. Always open, forever quiet.

customVenues.name: Dove Stone Reservoir Circular
customVenues.address: Start: Dovestone car park, Bank Lane, Greenfield
customVenues.blurb: The classic Saddleworth leg-stretcher: a flat, surfaced loop around the water with the gritstone edges towering over you. Pushchair and wheelchair friendly; herons guaranteed, ice cream van likely.

customVenues.name: Pots & Pans and the Obelisk
customVenues.blurb: Up through the lanes past St Chad's to the war memorial on Pots & Pans rock — the best view in the borough, from Winter Hill to Kinder on a clear day. Steep in places; earn your pint back at the Cross Keys.

customVenues.name: The Delph Donkey
customVenues.address: Start: Uppermill (or Delph — it works both ways)
customVenues.blurb: The old branch-line railway path from Uppermill to Delph, named after the train that once pottered along it. Flat, traffic-free and pram-friendly, with Dobcross on a hill above you all the way.

customVenues.name: Canal Towpath: Greenfield to Diggle
customVenues.address: Start: Well-i-Hole bridge, Greenfield (or any village on the way)
customVenues.blurb: The Huddersfield Narrow Canal through the whole valley — locks, herons, narrowboats and three villages' worth of pubs and cafés, ending at the mouth of the Standedge Tunnel. Grandpa Greene's is conveniently at the two-thirds mark.

customVenues.name: Standedge and the Boat Horse Road
customVenues.blurb: Follow the path the boat horses took over the moor while their narrowboats were legged through the tunnel beneath your feet. Wild, windy and wonderful — turn back at the cutting or carry on to Marsden and get the train home through the hill.

customVenues.name: Castleshaw Roman Fort Circular
customVenues.blurb: Out of Delph and up the Castleshaw valley to the Roman fort above the reservoirs - nineteen centuries of watching the pass over Standedge, and still the best picnic spot in the north of the parish.

customVenues.name: Chew Valley to Chew Reservoir
customVenues.blurb: The steady climb up the old tramway road into the Chew Valley, between crags to the highest-built reservoir of its day in England. A proper lungful of Pennine air; boggy at the top after rain.

customVenues.name: Uppermill to Brownhill Riverside Loop
customVenues.blurb: The gentle family one: canal towpath out to the visitor centre at Brownhill Bridge, back along the Tame through the park. Ducks to feed, trains to wave at, and a playground finish.

customVenues.name: Wharmton & the Mast
customVenues.blurb: The green whaleback hill that splits the valley in two, topped by the TV mast you can see from every village - the landmark that tells Saddleworth people they are nearly home.

customVenues.name: Castleshaw Reservoirs
customVenues.blurb: Two quiet reservoirs in a fold of the moors between Delph and Standedge, ringed by a gentle waterside path - herons, curlews, and a Roman fort on the shoulder above.

customVenues.name: Pots & Pans Obelisk
customVenues.blurb: The war memorial on its gritstone crag above Uppermill - the whole of Saddleworth at your feet, and the weathered rock basins that gave the hill its name.

customVenues.name: Standedge Tunnel Portal
customVenues.blurb: The Diggle mouth of the longest, highest, deepest canal tunnel in Britain - three and a quarter miles under the moor to Marsden, dug by hand over seventeen years.

customVenues.name: Saddleworth Viaduct
customVenues.blurb: Stone arches striding across the Tame since 1849, with the canal threading underneath - best admired from the towpath with an ice cream.

customVenues.name: Alphin Pike & the Indian’s Head
customVenues.blurb: The dark gritstone edges brooding over Dovestone - Alphin Pike, Wimberry Rocks and the profile locals call the Indian’s Head. Proper moorland: go shod and watered.

customVenues.name: St Chad’s Church
customVenues.blurb: Saddleworth’s parish church, up on the hillside since 1215 — the Rushcart ends here every August with hymns and a gurning contest, and the Church Inn waits a little way down the lane.

customVenues.name: Springhead Cricket Club
customVenues.blurb: Cricket at Mayfield Avenue since the 1880s, with a friendly clubhouse bar and junior sections.

customVenues.name: Delph & Dobcross Cricket & Bowling Club
customVenues.blurb: Cricket and crown-green bowls at the south end of the village — and the home of Delph’s Party in the Park each September.

customVenues.name: Nurture Saddleworth
customVenues.address: Top floor, Queen Anne’s Gallery, 64 High Street, Uppermill OL3 6HA
customVenues.blurb: Yoga, pilates, qigong and strength classes in a calm studio above the High Street — mornings and evenings most days.
customVenues.hours: Classes Mo-Th mornings & evenings; Su morning — timetable online

customVenues.name: Dobcross Band & Social Club
customVenues.blurb: Home of the Dobcross Silver Band, the youth and training bands — and a floodlit crown green where eleven league bowls teams play most evenings in season.

customVenues.name: Heights Chapel
customVenues.blurb: The lonely 1765 chapel on the hill above Delph — whitewashed, galleried, and one of the finest viewpoints in the parish. Occasional services and concerts.

customVenues.name: St Anne’s Church, Lydgate
customVenues.blurb: Lydgate’s hilltop church of 1788, its tower a landmark for miles across the Tame valley.

customVenues.name: Holy Trinity Church, Dobcross
customVenues.blurb: The 1787 village church above Dobcross Square, at the heart of the conservation village.

customVenues.name: St Thomas’ Church, Friarmere
customVenues.blurb: Friarmere’s parish church, rebuilt in 1765 on land the monks of Roche Abbey once farmed.

customVenues.name: Christ Church, Denshaw
customVenues.blurb: Denshaw’s 1863 church, spire against the moor at the meeting of the old turnpikes.

customVenues.name: St Mary’s Church, Greenfield
customVenues.blurb: Greenfield’s parish church of 1875, gateway to the Chew Valley.

customVenues.name: Play2 Diggle
customVenues.address: Robinson Works, Warth Mill, Huddersfield Road, Diggle OL3 5PJ
customVenues.blurb: Saddleworth’s own soft play — baby and toddler zone plus a big frame and ball court for the under-11s. No booking needed.

customVenues.name: Little Village Saddleworth
customVenues.address: Oakdale Mill, Delph New Road, Delph OL3 5BY
customVenues.blurb: An indoor pretend-play village — little shops, jobs and imaginations running wild. Two-hour sessions at 10:00, 13:00 and 16:00; book ahead at weekends.

customVenues.name: Uppermill Library
customVenues.address: St Chad’s, High Street, Uppermill OL3 6AP
customVenues.blurb: The village library — books, local history and free children’s sessions.

customVenues.name: Uppermill Methodist Church
customVenues.blurb: A busy community hub — toddler group, the 20th Oldham Scout Group, concerts and the summer music festival.

customVenues.name: Greenfield Methodist Church
customVenues.blurb: Chapel and hall on Chew Valley Road — home of the Jelly Tots baby & toddler group (Friday mornings in the lower hall).

customVenues.name: Kilngreen Church Hall
customVenues.blurb: Diggle’s church hall — base of the 4th Oldham Scout Group.

customVenues.name: Greenfield Primary School (halls)
customVenues.blurb: Out of hours, home to the Saddleworth Ballet School’s Saturday timetable.

customVenues.name: Evade Martial Arts
customVenues.address: Unit E207 Warmco Industrial Estate, Manchester Road, Mossley OL5 9AY
customVenues.blurb: Kickboxing, karate and BJJ just over the Greenfield border — Little Ninjas classes for 4–7s most days.

customVenues.name: Saddleworth School
customVenues.blurb: The valley-bottom secondary school at Diggle — out of hours its hall and pitches host everything from Rock Choir rehearsals to junior football academies.

customVenues.name: Tanners Dam
customVenues.blurb: Diggle Angling Club's water since 1952 — a mill lodge stocked with carp, tench, chub and ide (500lb of fresh carp went in, February 2026). Members only, no day tickets: seniors £55, under-16s £25, over-65s £45 — forms via diggleac.co.uk.

customVenues.name: Nine Lives
customVenues.address: The Greenfield Centre, Wellington Road, Greenfield, OL3 7AQ
customVenues.blurb: Neighbourhood café and sandwich shop inside the Greenfield Centre on Wellington Road — breakfasts, butties and cakes, Tuesday to Sunday.

customVenues.name: Hot Duck
customVenues.blurb: Dim sum and Cantonese plates upstairs at 26a High Street, from the family behind Hei Hei below.

customVenues.name: Bay Leaf
customVenues.blurb: Delph's Indian on King Street — curries a few doors from the Swan.

customVenues.name: Tunnel End Pie Co
customVenues.blurb: Award-winning pies baked behind the High Street — order ahead by phone or email (07415 526457) and collect weekday lunchtimes.

customVenues.name: Dobcross Village Store & Post Office
customVenues.blurb: The village store and post office on Woods Lane — takeaway coffee, a continental deli counter and the village noticeboard all in one.

customVenues.name: The Top House
customVenues.blurb: Springhead local up on Co-operative Street — pool table busy on league nights, with Top House A and B flying the flag in the Saddleworth Pool League.

customVenues.name: The Shawside
customVenues.blurb: Clubhouse pub up Grains Road on the Shaw fringe — four Shawside sides (A, B, C and C2) rack up across its two tables in the Saddleworth Pool League.

events.title: Partial Solar Eclipse over Saddleworth
events.description: Tonight the moon takes a huge bite out of the sun, low in the western sky — around nine-tenths covered at maximum. The tops make a grand grandstand; Pots & Pans faces the right way. NEVER look at the sun without proper eclipse glasses — sunglasses are not enough.

events.title: Partial Lunar Eclipse — Copper Moon over Dove Stone
events.description: A fortnight after the solar eclipse, the Earth’s shadow takes a deep bite out of the full moon in the small hours — most of the disc turning dusky copper as it sinks toward the western moors. Dove Stone’s dark skies are the best seat in the parish; no glasses needed for this one, just a flask.
